docs.title: MIMOSA: Integrated Assessment Model for Cost-Benefit Analysis
docs.text:
Documentation Installation Running Dashboard

MIMOSA is an Integrated Assessment Model (IAM) part of the IMAGE family, with 26 regions covering the whole world. It is a relatively simple Cost-Benefit IAM that still covers the relevant technological and socio-economic dynamics. The climate impacts are calculated using state-of-the-art COACCH damage functions, and the mitigation costs have been directly calibrated to the IPCC AR6 WGIII database.

MIMOSA is being developed at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development at Utrecht University, and is part of the IMAGE modelling framework.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
The model is written in the Python optimisation package Pyomo. It uses IPOPT (an open-source large-scale nonlinear optimisation suite) to solve the model.

Schematic overview of the MIMOSA model. Adapted from [1].

docs.text: When using MIMOSA, please cite [1] (global version) and [2] (regional version).

[2] van der Wijst, KI., Bosello, F., Dasgupta, S. et al. New damage curves and multimodel analysis suggest lower optimal temperature. Nature Climate Change 13, 434–441 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-023-01636-1

docs.title: What does MIMOSA stand for?
docs.text: MIMOSA: Mathematical Integrated Model for Optimal and Stylised Assessment

docs.title: Installing MIMOSA
docs.text:
MIMOSA is written in Python, and can be installed using pip: 

pip install mimosa

If you don't have Python installed yet, we highly recommend to use Anaconda to install python.

docs.title: Installing the optimisation engine IPOPT
docs.text:
Since MIMOSA is an optimisation model, an optimisation engine needs to be specified. We use the open-source optimisation engine IPOPT, which can be installed as a conda package.

On WindowsOn MacOSOn Linux 
conda install -c conda-forge ipopt>=3.14.17

conda install -c idaes-pse -c conda-forge idaes-pse

conda install -c conda-forge ipopt

conda install -c conda-forge ipopt

Once IPOPT is installed, you can now solve your MIMOSA runs (see Running MIMOSA): 

from mimosa import MIMOSA, load_params

params = load_params()

model1 = MIMOSA(params)
model1.solve()
model1.save("run1")

Fixing the error IPOPT not found on Windows

Sometimes, installing IPOPT with conda fails on Windows. To fix it, go to https://github.com/coin-or/Ipopt/releases and download the latest win64-version. Unzip the files. A subfolder bin should contain the file ipopt.exe. The next step is to add this folder to your PATH environment: Windows > Edit the system environment variables > Environment variables... > Select "Path" and click Edit... > Click New and browse to the folder you just unzipped. Make sure to select the bin subfolder as this folder contains the file ipopt.exe.

  1. Once you've downloaded the zip file of the latest win64-version on the coin website (currently Ipopt-3.14.15-win64-msvs2019-md.zip), unzip this file to folder of your choice. In the unzipped folder, there should be a bin folder.
  2. The next step is to tell Windows to look for IPOPT in this bin directory. This is achieved by adding the relevant folder to the environment path of Windows. Click on Start (or press the Win key), type environment and press Enter. This should open the dialog Edit the system environment variables.
  3. Click on Environment variables, select Path and click edit.
  4. Here, you can add the folder with the IPOPT bin folder. Click on New and add the folder you unzipped IPOPT in, making sure to select the sub-folder bin:
  5. You can test if everything works by opening an Anaconda Prompt and typing ipopt. It should show something like this:
Running MIMOSA without local computations

If you don't want to install IPOPT on your computer, you can also use the NEOS server (https://neos-server.org) to run MIMOSA remotely. This way, the installation of IPOPT is not required. This can be useful if you don't want to use your own computer to do the runs. However, this is typically much slower than installing IPOPT locally.

First, on the NEOS website, sign up for a free account. You can then run MIMOSA with NEOS enabled by simply providing it with the email address you used to sign up for NEOS:

from mimosa import MIMOSA, load_params

params = load_params()

model1 = MIMOSA(params)
# Change "your.email@email.com" to your the email address you used to sign up for NEOS
model1.solve(use_neos=True, neos_email="your.email@email.com") 
model1.save("run1")

Depending on the MIMOSA parameters chosen and on how busy the NEOS server is, running the model might take a while (typically a couple of minutes).

Next: Running MIMOSA

docs.title: Configurable parameters
docs.text:
SSP

SSP, used for population, baseline GDP and baseline emissions

  • Type: enum

  • Default: SSP2

  • Allowed values:

    • SSP1
    • SSP2
    • SSP3
    • SSP4
    • SSP5

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["SSP"] = "SSP2"
model = MIMOSA(params)
regionstype

Name of the region definition. Used in the mapping of the regional parameters.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: IMAGE26

  • Allowed values:

    • IMAGE26
    • SSP5
    • World

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["regionstype"] = "IMAGE26"
model = MIMOSA(params)
regionsmappings

List of region types and their conversion tables. Only used for regional parameters, not for aggregating or disaggregating variables or other output.

  • Type: list

  • Default: [{'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'COACCH', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_COACCH.csv'}, {'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'ADRICE2010', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_ADRICE2010.csv'}, {'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'ADRICE2012', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_ADRICE2012.csv'}]

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["regionsmappings"] = [{'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'COACCH', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_COACCH.csv'}, {'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'ADRICE2010', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_ADRICE2010.csv'}, {'regionstype1': 'IMAGE26', 'regionstype2': 'ADRICE2012', 'conversiontable': 'inputdata/regions/IMAGE26_ADRICE2012.csv'}]
model = MIMOSA(params)
regional_parameter_files

Dictionary of regional parameter files. If the regionstype of the file is different from the regionstype of the model, the file is converted using the regionsmappings parameter.

  • Type: dict

  • Default: {'economics': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/economics.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'MAC': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/mac.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'COACCH': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/COACCH.csv', 'regionstype': 'COACCH'}, 'ACCREU': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/ACCREU.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'ACCREU_CGE': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/ACCREU_CGE.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}}

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["regional_parameter_files"] = {'economics': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/economics.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'MAC': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/mac.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'COACCH': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/COACCH.csv', 'regionstype': 'COACCH'}, 'ACCREU': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/ACCREU.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}, 'ACCREU_CGE': {'filename': 'inputdata/regionalparams/ACCREU_CGE.csv', 'regionstype': 'IMAGE26'}}
model = MIMOSA(params)
regions

Dictionary of all regions with optional dictionaries defining, optionally, manual values for certain parameters for that specific region.

  • Type: dict

  • Default: {'CAN': None, 'USA': None, 'MEX': None, 'RCAM': None, 'BRA': None, 'RSAM': None, 'NAF': None, 'WAF': None, 'EAF': None, 'SAF': None, 'WEU': None, 'CEU': None, 'TUR': None, 'UKR': None, 'STAN': None, 'RUS': None, 'ME': None, 'INDIA': None, 'KOR': None, 'CHN': None, 'SEAS': None, 'INDO': None, 'JAP': None, 'OCE': None, 'RSAS': None, 'RSAF': None}

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["regions"] = {'CAN': None, 'USA': None, 'MEX': None, 'RCAM': None, 'BRA': None, 'RSAM': None, 'NAF': None, 'WAF': None, 'EAF': None, 'SAF': None, 'WEU': None, 'CEU': None, 'TUR': None, 'UKR': None, 'STAN': None, 'RUS': None, 'ME': None, 'INDIA': None, 'KOR': None, 'CHN': None, 'SEAS': None, 'INDO': None, 'JAP': None, 'OCE': None, 'RSAS': None, 'RSAF': None}
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: time
docs.text:
start

Year in which the model starts

  • Type: int

  • Default: 2025

  • Min: 1900

  • Max: 2100

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["time"]["start"] = 2025
model = MIMOSA(params)
end

Last year of the model run

  • Type: int

  • Default: 2150

  • Min: 1901

  • Max: 2300

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["time"]["end"] = 2150
model = MIMOSA(params)
dt

Initial timestep length in years

  • Type: float

  • Default: 5

  • Min: 0.5

  • Max: 20

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["time"]["dt"] = 5
model = MIMOSA(params)
periods

Optional timestep changes, mapping each change year to the timestep length in years used after that year

  • Type: dict

  • Default: {2050: 10}

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["time"]["periods"] = {2050: 10}
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: economics
docs.text:
PRTP

Pure rate of time preference

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.015

  • Min: 0

  • Max: 0.2

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["PRTP"] = 0.015
model = MIMOSA(params)
elasmu

Elasticity of marginal utility

  • Type: float

  • Default: 1.001

  • Min: 0.1

  • Max: 10

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["elasmu"] = 1.001
model = MIMOSA(params)
inequal_aversion

Parameter of inequality aversion. Should be between 0 and elasmu. Only used when model structure - welfare module is inequal_aversion_general

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.5

  • Min: 0.0

  • Max: 3

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["inequal_aversion"] = 0.5
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: economics > GDP
docs.text:
alpha

Output elasticity of capital

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.3

  • Min: 0

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["GDP"]["alpha"] = 0.3
model = MIMOSA(params)
depreciation of capital

Yearly depreciation rate of capital stock

  • Type: float

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["GDP"]["depreciation of capital"] = 0.05
model = MIMOSA(params)
savings rate

Fraction of GDP used for investments

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.21

  • Min: 0

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["GDP"]["savings rate"] = 0.21

docs.title: economics > MAC
docs.text:
beta

Power factor of the MAC curve

  • Type: float

  • Default: 3

  • Min: 0.01

  • Max: 10

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["beta"] = 3
model = MIMOSA(params)
gamma

Calibration level of the MAC (carbon price for 100% reduction)

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: 2887 USD2010/tCO2

  • Unit: currency_unit/emissionsrate_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["gamma"] = "2887 USD2010/tCO2"
model = MIMOSA(params)
LBD_rate

Learning by doing rate: reduction in marginal mitigation costs for doubling cumulative mitigation capacity. Empirical studies show values between 0.65 (high learning) and 0.95 (low learning)

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.82

  • Min: 0.1

  • Max: 1

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["LBD_rate"] = 0.82
model = MIMOSA(params)
LBD_scaling

Scaling factor for learning by doing to transform the units of cumulative mitigation in relative terms (compared to baseline emissions in t=0). Only used for calibration, and should not be used to change the amount of LBD (for this, use economics > MAC > LBD_rate)

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: 40 GtCO2

  • Unit: emissions_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["LBD_scaling"] = "40 GtCO2"
model = MIMOSA(params)
LOT_rate

Learning rate of exogenous learning (learning over time). By default, there is no exogenous learning assumed, as all the technological learning happens endogenously (learning by doing).

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0

  • Min: 0

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["LOT_rate"] = 0
model = MIMOSA(params)
regional calibration factor

Column from mac.csv to be used for the regional MACs. The MACs are calibrated from TIMER SSP2-RCP2.6 MACs at a given year and a given carbon price / abatement level.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: kappa_rel_abatement_0.75_2050

  • Allowed values:

    • kappa_carbonprice_200_2030
    • kappa_carbonprice_200_2050
    • kappa_carbonprice_200_2070
    • kappa_carbonprice_200_2100
    • kappa_carbonprice_300_2030
    • kappa_carbonprice_300_2050
    • kappa_carbonprice_300_2070
    • kappa_carbonprice_300_2100
    • kappa_carbonprice_500_2030
    • kappa_carbonprice_500_2050
    • kappa_carbonprice_500_2070
    • kappa_carbonprice_500_2100
    • kappa_carbonprice_1000_2030
    • kappa_carbonprice_1000_2050
    • kappa_carbonprice_1000_2070
    • kappa_carbonprice_1000_2100
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.25_2030
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.25_2050
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.25_2070
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.25_2100
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.4_2030
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.4_2050
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.4_2070
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.4_2100
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.5_2050
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.5_2070
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.5_2100
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.75_2050
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.75_2070
    • kappa_rel_abatement_0.75_2100

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["regional calibration factor"] = "kappa_rel_abatement_0.75_2050"
model = MIMOSA(params)
rel_mitigation_costs_min_level

Minimum level of mitigation costs (rel to GDP). By default, this is 0: no negative attributed mitigation costs are allowed. For certain effort-sharing regimes, this value can become negative to allow certain (small) financial transfers.

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0

  • Min: -2

  • Max: 0

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = 0
model = MIMOSA(params)

economics > emission trade
docs.text:
min rel payment level

Which percentage of the area under the MAC of a region should it pay itself (minimum)? If false: no limt

  • Type: float

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: 0

  • Max: 1

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["emission trade"]["min rel payment level"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)
max rel payment level

Which percentage of the area under the MAC of a region should it pay itself (maximum)? If false: no limit

  • Type: float

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: 1

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["emission trade"]["max rel payment level"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: economics > damages
docs.text:
percentage reversible

Factor of damages that are reversible

  • Type: float

  • Default: 1

  • Min: 0

  • Max: 1

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["percentage reversible"] = 1
model = MIMOSA(params)
scale factor

Manual scaling factor to increase or decrease damages

  • Type: float

  • Default: 1

  • Min: -inf

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["scale factor"] = 1
model = MIMOSA(params)
ignore damages

Flag to not take into account the damages in the GDP (but damages are calculated)

  • Type: bool

  • Default: False

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["ignore damages"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)
quantile

Damage quantile (Only used for COACCH)

  • Type: enum

  • Default: 0.5

  • Allowed values:

    • 0.025
    • 0.05
    • 0.16
    • 0.25
    • 0.33
    • 0.5
    • 0.67
    • 0.75
    • 0.84
    • 0.95
    • 0.975

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["quantile"] = 0.5
model = MIMOSA(params)
coacch_slr_withadapt

Flag to use the SLR-with-Adapation damage functions (Only used for COACCH)

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["coacch_slr_withadapt"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
coacch_combined_slr_nonslr_damages

If true, do not model SLR damages separately from non-SLR, but use the combined damage functions (Only used for COACCH)

  • Type: bool

  • Default: False

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["coacch_combined_slr_nonslr_damages"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: economics > damages > accreu
docs.text:
adaptation

Enable sector-specific adaptation with "sectoral", disable it with "noadaptation", or use "combined" labour productivity and riverine flooding adaptation for diagnostics and model comparisons.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: noadaptation

  • Allowed values:

    • sectoral
    • combined
    • noadaptation

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["adaptation"] = "noadaptation"
model = MIMOSA(params)
cba_strategy

How solve() coordinates mitigation and adaptation in an ACCREU cost-benefit analysis. The sequential strategy first optimises mitigation without adaptation and then calculates analytical optimal adaptation for that pathway. The joint strategy uses the ordinary one-model solve path, with adaptation either chosen by the solver or determined analytically.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: mitigation_then_adaptation

  • Allowed values:

    • mitigation_then_adaptation
    • joint

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["cba_strategy"] = "mitigation_then_adaptation"
model = MIMOSA(params)
adaptation_determination

How ACCREU adaptation expenditure is determined. With solver_control it is a free optimisation or simulation control. With analytical_optimum it is calculated from the analytical optimal-adaptation equation.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: analytical_optimum

  • Allowed values:

    • solver_control
    • analytical_optimum

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["adaptation_determination"] = "analytical_optimum"
model = MIMOSA(params)
adaptation_calibration

Calibration of the sectoral ACCREU adaptation curves. "accreu" uses the original source-model coefficients. The three "literature" options use realised-effectiveness caps and cost multipliers calibrated to the low, central, and high ends of literature benefit-cost ranges at a 5% discount rate. They apply to both separate and combined adaptation.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: accreu

  • Allowed values:

    • accreu
    • literature_low
    • literature
    • literature_high

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["adaptation_calibration"] = "accreu"
model = MIMOSA(params)
monetise_mortality

Flag for whether the mortality should be monetised using the SVL (Statistical Value of Life)

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["monetise_mortality"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
mortality_vsl_rel_gdp_cap

If the monetise_mortality option is enabled, use this value for the Statistical Value of Life (SVL), expressed as multiple of GDP per capita. Note: while this assumes a global value of the SVL in relative terms, the dollar value of the SVL differs per country. This has ethical implications.

  • Type: float

  • Default: 117.59

  • Min: -inf

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["mortality_vsl_rel_gdp_cap"] = 117.59
model = MIMOSA(params)
adaptation_effectiveness_scale_factor

Scales the max. effectiveness factor for the sectoral adaptation. Used to analyse the effects of a less effective adaptation.

  • Type: float

  • Default: 1

  • Min: 0

  • Max: 1

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["adaptation_effectiveness_scale_factor"] = 1
model = MIMOSA(params)
delay_adaptation_until_year

Delays adaptation until after this given year. If false, no constraint on adaptation is set.

  • Type: int

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: 2030

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["economics"]["damages"]["accreu"]["delay_adaptation_until_year"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: emissions
docs.text:
carbonbudget

Value of the carbon budget. Example: "800 GtCO2" (the unit is important). If set to False, no carbon budget is imposed: this is cost-benefit mode. Default: False.

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Unit: emissions_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)
global min level

Limit on the emission level (globally), mostly used for negative emissions. Can also be false, then no limit is imposed

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: -20 GtCO2/yr

  • Can be false: yes

  • Unit: emissionsrate_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["global min level"] = "-20 GtCO2/yr"
model = MIMOSA(params)
regional min level

Limit on the emission level (per region), mostly used for negative emissions. Can also be false, then no limit is imposed

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: -10 GtCO2/yr

  • Can be false: yes

  • Unit: emissionsrate_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["regional min level"] = "-10 GtCO2/yr"
model = MIMOSA(params)
not positive after budget year

If true, impose net-zero emissions after budget year (2100)

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["not positive after budget year"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
non increasing emissions after 2100

If true, the regional emissions after 2100 are not allowed to climb.

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["non increasing emissions after 2100"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
baseline carbon intensity

If true, use baseline carbon intensity to calculate baseline emissions. If false, the SSP baseline emissions are used, regardless of lower GDP.

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["baseline carbon intensity"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
cumulative_emissions_trapz

If true, calculate cumulative emissions using trapezoidal interpolation. If false, cum. emissions are simply cum_emissions[t-1] + dt * cum_emissions[t]. This is less accurate, but better for numerical stability. For small dt the approximation is usually still acceptable.

  • Type: bool

  • Default: True

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["cumulative_emissions_trapz"] = True
model = MIMOSA(params)
delay_mitigation_until_year

Delays mitigation until after this given year. If false, mitigation is always available.

  • Type: int

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: 2030

  • Max: inf

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["delay_mitigation_until_year"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: emissions > pulse
docs.text:
year

Year in which an exogenous CO2 pulse is released

  • Type: int

  • Default: 2025

Example usage: 

params = load_params()

Exogenous CO2 pulse added directly to cumulative emissions

  • Type: quantity

docs.title: emissions > inertia
docs.text:
global

Maximum reduction speed, in % of initial emissions (should be negative) Can also be false, then no inertia limit is imposed

  • Type: float

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: -inf

  • Max: 0

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["inertia"]["global"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)
regional

Maximum reduction speed, in % of initial emissions (should be negative) Can also be false, then no inertia limit is imposed

  • Type: float

  • Default: -0.05

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: -inf

  • Max: 0

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["emissions"]["inertia"]["regional"] = -0.05
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: effort sharing
docs.text:
percapconv_year

Year of convergence to per capita emission allowance (only used when model structure - effortsharing module is per_cap_convergence) Can also be false, then always use grandfathering

  • Type: float

  • Default: 2050

  • Can be false: yes

  • Min: 2020

  • Max: 2200

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["effort sharing"]["percapconv_year"] = 2050
model = MIMOSA(params)
ecpc_discount_rate

Discount rate for historical debt in the ECPC effort sharing regime (Equal Cumulative Per Capita regime). Only used when model structure - effortsharing module is equal_cumulative_per_cap

  • Type: float

  • Default: 0.03

  • Min: 0

  • Max: 1

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_discount_rate"] = 0.03
model = MIMOSA(params)
ecpc_start_year

Start year for historical debt in the ECPC effort sharing regime (Equal Cumulative Per Capita regime). Only used when model structure - effortsharing module is equal_cumulative_per_cap

  • Type: float

  • Default: 1850

  • Min: 1800

  • Max: 2019

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_start_year"] = 1850
model = MIMOSA(params)
ecpc_repayment_endyear

Year at which the repayment of the historical emission debt should be finished in the ECPC effort sharing regime. Before this year, the debt repayment is lowered linearly.

Can also be false: then the historical debt repayment is spread out equally over every time period.

- Type: float

- Default: 2050

- Can be false: yes



- Min: 2030

- Max: 2150



Example usage:


```python hl_lines="2"
params = load_params()
params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_repayment_endyear"] = 2050
model = MIMOSA(params)
```

docs.title: temperature
docs.text:
initial

Temperature in initial year of model run (2025 by default).

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: 1.27 delta_degC

  • Unit: temperature_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["temperature"]["initial"] = "1.27 delta_degC"
model = MIMOSA(params)
TCRE

Transient Climate Response to CO2 Emissions

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: 0.62 delta_degC/(TtCO2)

  • Unit: (temperature_unit)/(emissions_unit)

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["temperature"]["TCRE"] = "0.62 delta_degC/(TtCO2)"
model = MIMOSA(params)
target

Temperature target in 2100 (and beyond). Can also be false, then no temperature target is imposed

  • Type: quantity

  • Default: False

  • Can be false: yes

  • Unit: temperature_unit

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["temperature"]["target"] = False
model = MIMOSA(params)

docs.title: sealevelrise
docs.text:
projection

Deterministic sea-level-rise parameter set. The central set represents an AR6-calibrated central response; low represents the lower part of the AR6 likely range, and high is a low-likelihood, high-impact sensitivity case. All sets share the same historical initial conditions.

  • Type: enum

  • Default: central

  • Allowed values:

    • low
    • central
    • high

Example usage: 

params = load_params()
params["sealevelrise"]["projection"] = "central"
model = MIMOSA(params)

params = load_params()

params = load_params()

docs.title: All variables
docs.text:
GDP_gross

Regional gross GDP from the Cobb-Douglas production function, before deducting damages, adaptation costs, mitigation costs, and financial transfers.

  • Units: usd*trillion/yr
  • Dimensions: t, regions

GDP_loss

Regional GDP loss relative to the baseline, calculated as baseline GDP minus net GDP, divided by baseline GDP. Includes direct costs and indirect effects on economic growth.

  • Units: fraction_of_baseline_GDP
  • Dimensions: t, regions

GDP_net

Regional net GDP available for investment and consumption after mitigation costs, financial transfers, and any included damage and adaptation costs.

  • Units: usd*trillion/yr
  • Dimensions: t, regions

LBD_factor

Multiplier on marginal abatement costs from learning by doing, based on cumulative emissions avoided relative to the SSP baseline through the preceding timestep. Starts at one; lower values mean cheaper mitigation.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

LOT_factor

Multiplier on marginal abatement costs from exogenous technological progress, independent of mitigation undertaken. Starts at one; a positive learning rate reduces it at each model timestep.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

NPV

Regional stock of productive capital. Increases through investment and decreases through depreciation; used in the Cobb-Douglas production function.

consumption

damage_costs

damage_costs_abs

Total damages from all sectors (excluding non-market impacts like mortality), in currency units.

damage_costs_abs

Total regional COACCH damage costs in currency units, calculated as the damage fraction times gross GDP.

domestic_mitigation_costs_abs

Cost of emission reductions physically carried out in a region, calculated as the area under its marginal abatement cost curve times baseline emissions.

effort_sharing_common_level

Common mitigation-cost share of gross GDP targeted across regions. Each region's attributed mitigation-cost share is constrained to remain approximately equal to this value.

Available when:

financial_transfer

global_GDP_gross

Global gross GDP, calculated as the sum of regional gross GDP.

  • Units: usd*trillion/yr
  • Dimensions: t

global_GDP_loss

Global GDP loss relative to the baseline, calculated as global baseline GDP minus global net GDP, divided by global baseline GDP.

global_cost_per_emission_reduction_unit

Average global mitigation cost per unit of CO2 emission reduction, calculated as total mitigation costs divided by total regional emission reductions. Set to zero at the initial timestep.

  • Units: usd*trillion/GtCO2
  • Dimensions: t

global_cumulative_emissions

Cumulative global net CO2 emissions since the model start, including any exogenous emissions pulse. Calculated using trapezoidal integration or timestep-weighted summation, depending on configuration.

  • Units: GtCO2
  • Dimensions: t

global_damage_costs

Global total damages from all sectors (excluding non-market impacts like mortality), as a fraction of global GDP.

  • Units: fraction_of_GDP
  • Dimensions: t

global_damage_costs

Global COACCH damage costs as a fraction of global gross GDP, calculated from the sum of regional damage costs in currency units.

  • Units: fraction_of_GDP
  • Dimensions: t

global_emission_reduction_per_cost_unit

Average global CO2 emission reduction per unit of mitigation spending, calculated as total regional emission reductions divided by total mitigation costs. Set to zero at the initial timestep.

  • Units: GtCO2/usd/trillion
  • Dimensions: t

global_emissions

Global net CO2 emissions, calculated as the sum of regional net emissions. Negative values represent net CO2 removal.

  • Units: GtCO2/yr
  • Dimensions: t

global_indirect_costs

Global GDP loss beyond direct costs, calculated as global GDP loss minus total direct costs divided by global baseline GDP.

  • Units: fraction_of_baseline_GDP
  • Dimensions: t

global_mitigation_costs

Global mitigation costs as a fraction of global gross GDP, calculated from the sum of regional mitigation costs.

  • Units: fraction_of_GDP
  • Dimensions: t

global_relative_cumulative_emissions

Cumulative global CO2 emissions divided by cumulative SSP baseline emissions since the model start. Set to one at the initial timestep.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

global_welfare

Undiscounted global welfare at each timestep, calculated as the sum of regional per-capita utilities weighted by population.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

global_welfare

Undiscounted global welfare, calculated by applying the utility function to global per-capita consumption after non-market damages and multiplying by global population.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

global_welfare

Undiscounted global welfare, calculated by aggregating regional welfare contributions with the configured inequality aversion and elasticity of marginal utility.

  • Units: not declared
  • Dimensions: t

indirect_costs

Regional GDP loss beyond direct costs, expressed as a fraction of baseline GDP. Includes effects of reduced capital accumulation.

  • Units: fraction_of_baseline_GDP
  • Dimensions: t, regions

investments

Regional investment in productive capital, calculated as the fixed savings rate times net GDP.

utility

utility

utility

docs.text: The MIMOSA model consists of several sub-modules, called model components. Each component is made up of multiple variables (global or regional), parameters and equations (called constraints).

docs.title: Building the concrete model
docs.text:
Builds the concrete model for MIMOSA by combining all components. Some components are optional. In the parameters, different variants of some components can be chosen. The components are:

  • damage module: The damage module to use
  • emissiontrade module: The emission trading module to use
  • financialtransfer module: The financial transfer module to use
  • welfare module: The welfare module to use
  • objective module: The objective module to use
  • effortsharing module: The effort-sharing module to use

def create_model(
    inputs: ModelInputs,
) -> Tuple[ConcreteModel, List[Equation]]:
    """
    ## Building the concrete model

    Builds the concrete model for MIMOSA by combining all components. Some components are optional. In the
    parameters, different variants of some components can be chosen. The components are:

    - [`damage module`](#param__model%20structure.damage%20module): The damage module to use
    - [`emissiontrade module`](#param__model%20structure.emissiontrade%20module): The emission trading module to use
    - [`financialtransfer module`](#param__model%20structure.financialtransfer%20module): The financial transfer module to use
    - [`welfare module`](#param__model%20structure.welfare%20module): The welfare module to use
    - [`objective module`](#param__model%20structure.objective%20module): The objective module to use
    - [`effortsharing module`](#param__model%20structure.effortsharing%20module): The effort-sharing module to use

    """
    m = create_base_model(inputs)

    # Each constraint will be put in this list,
    # then added to the model at the end of this file.
    constraints = []

    # Emissions, temperature and sea-level rise
    constraints.extend(emissions.get_constraints(m, inputs))
    constraints.extend(sealevelrise.get_constraints(m, inputs))

    # Damage and mitigation costs
    constraints.extend(damages.get_constraints(m, inputs))
    constraints.extend(mitigation.get_constraints(m, inputs))

    # Emission trading, financial transfers and effort sharing
    constraints.extend(emissiontrade.get_constraints(m, inputs))
    constraints.extend(financialtransfer.get_constraints(m, inputs))
    constraints.extend(effortsharing.get_constraints(m, inputs))

    # Production, consumption and welfare
    constraints.extend(cobbdouglas.get_constraints(m, inputs))
    constraints.extend(welfare.get_constraints(m, inputs))

    # Objective of optimisation
    model_objective, objective_constraints = objective.get_constraints(m, inputs)
    constraints.extend(objective_constraints)

    ######################
    # Add constraints to concrete model
    ######################

    for constraint in constraints:
        add_constraint(m, constraint.to_pyomo_constraint(m), constraint.name)

    ######################
    # Get all equations (not constraints) for simulation mode
    ######################
    equations = [eq for eq in constraints if isinstance(eq, Equation)]

    m.objective = model_objective

    return m, equations

docs.title: Gross and net GDP
docs.text:
The core of the model is the economic module, detailing how GDP, investments and consumptions vary over time. We use a traditional Cobb-Douglas production function. This means that the gross GDP is calculated by:

$$ \href{./#var__GDP_gross}{\text{GDP}_{\text{gross},t,r}} = \href{./#param__timeandregional.TFP}{\text{TFP}_{t,r}} \cdot \href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{L}^{1-\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}}_{t,r} \cdot \left(\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}}\right)^{\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}}, $$ with \(\href{./#param__timeandregional.TFP}{\text{TFP}}\) the total factor productivity (exogenously calibrated from the baseline SSP scenarios) \(\href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{L}\) the labor (represented by the total population), \(\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K}\) the capital stock and \(\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}\) the share of capital in the production function.

Source code in mimosa/common/economics.py 
def calc_GDP(TFP, L, K, alpha):
    r"""
    $$ \href{./#var__GDP_gross}{\text{GDP}_{\text{gross},t,r}} = \href{./#param__timeandregional.TFP}{\text{TFP}\_{t,r}} \cdot \href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{L}^{1-\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}}\_{t,r} \cdot \left(\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K\_{t,r}}\right)^{\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}}, $$
    with $\href{./#param__timeandregional.TFP}{\text{TFP}}$ the total factor productivity (exogenously calibrated from the baseline SSP scenarios)
    $\href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{L}$ the labor (represented by the [total population](#param__timeandregional.population)), $\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K}$ the capital stock and $\href{./#param__economics.GDP.alpha}{\alpha}$ the share of capital in the production function.

    """
    return TFP * L ** (1 - alpha) * K**alpha

The net GDP is then calculated by subtracting the damages and mitigation costs from the gross GDP. The _abs variables are used here because the amounts subtracted from GDP must be in currency units.

\[ \begin{align} \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}} =\ & \href{./#var__GDP_gross}{\text{GDP}_{\text{gross},t,r}} \cdot (1 - \href{./#var__damage_costs}{\text{damage costs}_{t,r}}) \\ &\ \ \ - \href{./#var__mitigation_costs_abs}{\text{mitigation costs abs}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__financialtransfer_globaldamagepool::financial_transfer_abs}{\text{financial transfer abs}_{t,r}} \end{align} \]

The last term represents optional financial transfers to compensate regions for damage costs. By default this term is always 0 (see Financial transfers).

docs.title: Investments and consumption
docs.text:
This net GDP is then split in a part of investments (\(\href{./#var__investments}{I_t}\)) and a part of consumption (\(\href{./#var__consumption}{C_t}\)), according to a fixed savings rate (\(\href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}}\)):

\[ \href{./#var__investments}{I_{t,r}} = \href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}} \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}}, \] \[ \href{./#var__consumption}{C_{t,r}} = (1 - \href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}}) \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}}. \]

Consumption is physical consumption. Monetised non-market damages, such as mortality, are deducted separately in the welfare calculation.

docs.title: Capital stock
docs.text:
The capital stock \(\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_t}\) grows over time according to the investments and the depreciation of the capital stock:

\[ \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t-1,r}} + \Delta t \cdot \frac{\partial \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}}}{\partial t}, \]

with the change in capital stock calculated by:

\[ \frac{\partial \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}}}{\partial t} = \frac{1}{\Delta t} \cdot ((1 - \href{./#param__economics.GDP.depreciation of capital}{\text{dk}})^{\Delta t} - 1) \cdot \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}} + \href{./#var__investments}{I_{t,r}}.\] Source code in mimosa/common/economics.py 
def calc_dKdt(K, dk, I, dt):
    r"""
    $$ \frac{\partial \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}}}{\partial t} = \frac{1}{\Delta t} \cdot ((1 - \href{./#param__economics.GDP.depreciation of capital}{\text{dk}})^{\Delta t}  - 1) \cdot \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}} + \href{./#var__investments}{I_{t,r}}.$$
    """
    return ((1 - dk) ** dt - 1) / dt * K + I

Since this only gives the change in capital stock, we need to add the initial capital stock to get the actual capital stock. This is calculated as a region-dependent multiple of the initial GDP:

\[ \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t=0,r}} = \href{./#param__regional.economics.init_capital_factor}{\text{init_capitalstock_factor}_r} \cdot \href{./#param__timeandregional.baseline_GDP}{\text{GDP}_{t=0,r}}. \]

The regional initial capital stock factors are calibrated from capital-stock-to-GDP ratios in the IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset.

def get_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    r"""
    # Economic module and production function

    ## Gross and net GDP

    The core of the model is the economic module, detailing how GDP, investments and
    consumptions vary over time. We use a traditional Cobb-Douglas production function. This means
    that the gross GDP is calculated by:

    :::mimosa.common.economics.calc_GDP

    The net GDP is then calculated by subtracting the damages and
    mitigation costs from the gross GDP. The `_abs` variables are used here because the amounts
    subtracted from GDP must be in currency units.

    $$
    \begin{align}
    \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}} =\ & \href{./#var__GDP_gross}{\text{GDP}_{\text{gross},t,r}} \cdot (1 - \href{./#var__damage_costs}{\text{damage costs}_{t,r}}) \\
    &\ \ \ - \href{./#var__mitigation_costs_abs}{\text{mitigation costs abs}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__financialtransfer_globaldamagepool::financial_transfer_abs}{\text{financial transfer abs}_{t,r}}
    \end{align}
    $$

    The last term represents optional financial transfers to compensate regions for damage
    costs. By default this term is always 0 (see [Financial transfers](financialtransfers.md)).

    ## Investments and consumption

    This net GDP is then split in a part of investments ($\href{./#var__investments}{I_t}$) and a part of consumption ($\href{./#var__consumption}{C_t}$), according to a fixed savings rate ($\href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}}$):

    $$ \href{./#var__investments}{I_{t,r}} = \href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}} \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}}, $$

    $$ \href{./#var__consumption}{C_{t,r}} = (1 - \href{./#param__economics.GDP.savings rate}{\text{sr}}) \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net},t,r}}. $$

    Consumption is physical consumption. Monetised non-market damages, such as mortality,
    are deducted separately in the welfare calculation.

    ## Capital stock

    The capital stock $\href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_t}$ grows over time according to the investments and the depreciation of the capital stock:

    $$ \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t-1,r}} + \Delta t \cdot \frac{\partial \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t,r}}}{\partial t}, $$

    with the change in capital stock calculated by:

    :::mimosa.common.economics.calc_dKdt

    Since this only gives the change in capital stock, we need to add the initial capital stock to get the actual capital stock.
    This is calculated as a region-dependent multiple of the initial GDP:

    $$ \href{./#var__capital_stock}{K_{t=0,r}} = \href{./#param__regional.economics.init_capital_factor}{\text{init_capitalstock_factor}_r} \cdot \href{./#param__timeandregional.baseline_GDP}{\text{GDP}_{t=0,r}}. $$

    The [regional initial capital stock factors](#param__regional.economics.init_capital_factor) are calibrated from capital-stock-to-GDP ratios in
    the [IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset](https://data.imf.org/en/Datasets/ICSD).
    ``` plotly
    {"file_path": "./assets/plots/economics_init_capital_factor.json"}
    ```

    ## Parameters defined in this module
    - init_capitalstock_factor
    - params["economics"]["GDP"]["alpha"]: Output elasticity of capital. Type: float. Default: 0.3. Min: 0. Max: 1.
    - params["economics"]["GDP"]["depreciation of capital"]: Yearly depreciation rate of capital stock. Type: float. Default: 0.05. Min: 0. Max: inf.
    - params["economics"]["GDP"]["savings rate"]: Fraction of GDP used for investments. Type: float. Default: 0.21. Min: 0. Max: 1.
    - params["economics"]["damages"]["ignore damages"]: Flag to not take into account the damages in the GDP (but damages are calculated). Type: bool. Default: False.



    """
    constraints = []
    m.init_capitalstock_factor = Param(
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("dimensionless"),
        initialize=inputs.regional("economics", "init_capital_factor"),
    )
    m.capital_stock = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.init_capitalstock_factor[r] * m.baseline_GDP[t, r],
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Regional stock of productive capital. Increases through investment and decreases through depreciation; used in the Cobb-Douglas production function.",
    )

    # Parameters
    m.alpha = Param(initialize=inputs.config("economics.GDP.alpha"))
    m.dk = Param(initialize=inputs.config("economics.GDP.depreciation of capital"))
    m.sr = Param(initialize=inputs.config("economics.GDP.savings rate"))

    m.GDP_gross = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.baseline_GDP[0, r],
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Regional gross GDP from the Cobb-Douglas production function, before deducting damages, adaptation costs, mitigation costs, and financial transfers.",
    )
    m.global_GDP_gross = Var(
        m.t,
        initialize=lambda m, t: sum(m.baseline_GDP[t, r] for r in m.regions),
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Global gross GDP, calculated as the sum of regional gross GDP.",
    )
    m.GDP_net = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.baseline_GDP[0, r],
        doc="Regional net GDP available for investment and consumption after mitigation costs, financial transfers, and any included damage and adaptation costs.",
    )
    m.global_GDP_net = Var(
        m.t,
        initialize=lambda m, t: sum(m.baseline_GDP[t, r] for r in m.regions),
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Global net GDP, calculated as the sum of regional net GDP.",
    )
    m.investments = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Regional investment in productive capital, calculated as the fixed savings rate times net GDP.",
    )
    m.consumption = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        doc="Regional physical consumption, equal to net GDP minus investment.",
    )

    m.ignore_damages = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("economics.damages.ignore damages")
    )

    m.TFP = Param(m.t, m.regions, initialize=economics.get_TFP_value)

    # Cobb-Douglas, GDP, investments, capital and consumption
    constraints.extend(
        [
            RegionalEquation(
                m.capital_stock,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    m.capital_stock[t - 1, r]
                    + m.period_length[t]
                    * economics.calc_dKdt(
                        m.capital_stock[t - 1, r],
                        m.dk,
                        m.investments[t - 1, r],
                        m.period_length[t],
                    )
                    if t > 0
                    else m.init_capitalstock_factor[r] * m.baseline_GDP[0, r]
                ),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.GDP_gross,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    economics.calc_GDP(
                        m.TFP[t, r],
                        m.population[t, r],
                        soft_min(m.capital_stock[t, r], scale=10),
                        m.alpha,
                    )
                    if t > 0
                    else m.baseline_GDP[0, r]
                ),
            ),
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_GDP_gross,
                lambda m, t: sum(m.GDP_gross[t, r] for r in m.regions),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.GDP_net,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    m.GDP_gross[t, r]
                    * (
                        1
                        - (
                            (m.damage_costs[t, r] + m.adaptation_costs[t, r])
                            if not value(m.ignore_damages)
                            else 0
                        )
                    )
                    - m.mitigation_costs_abs[t, r]
                    - m.financial_transfer_abs[t, r]
                ),
            ),
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_GDP_net,
                lambda m, t: sum(m.GDP_net[t, r] for r in m.regions),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.investments,
                lambda m, t, r: m.sr * m.GDP_net[t, r],
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.consumption,
                lambda m, t, r: (1 - m.sr) * m.GDP_net[t, r],
            ),
        ]
    )

    # GDP loss: takes into account indirect effects of reduced GDP growth due to damages and mitigation costs
    m.GDP_loss = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_baseline_GDP"),
        initialize=0,
        doc="Regional GDP loss relative to the baseline, calculated as baseline GDP minus net GDP, divided by baseline GDP. Includes direct costs and indirect effects on economic growth.",
    )
    m.global_GDP_loss = Var(
        m.t,
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_baseline_GDP"),
        initialize=0,
        doc="Global GDP loss relative to the baseline, calculated as global baseline GDP minus global net GDP, divided by global baseline GDP.",
    )

    m.total_direct_costs_abs = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("currency_unit"),
        initialize=0,
        doc="Total regional direct costs in currency units: the sum of mitigation costs, damage costs, and adaptation costs.",
    )
    m.indirect_costs = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_baseline_GDP"),
        initialize=0,
        doc="Regional GDP loss beyond direct costs, expressed as a fraction of baseline GDP. Includes effects of reduced capital accumulation.",
    )
    m.global_indirect_costs = Var(
        m.t,
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_baseline_GDP"),
        initialize=0,
        doc="Global GDP loss beyond direct costs, calculated as global GDP loss minus total direct costs divided by global baseline GDP.",
    )

    constraints.extend(
        [
            RegionalEquation(
                m.GDP_loss,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    (m.baseline_GDP[t, r] - m.GDP_net[t, r]) / m.baseline_GDP[t, r]
                ),
            ),
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_GDP_loss,
                lambda m, t: (
                    (m.global_baseline_GDP[t] - m.global_GDP_net[t])
                    / m.global_baseline_GDP[t]
                ),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.total_direct_costs_abs,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    m.mitigation_costs_abs[t, r]
                    + m.damage_costs_abs[t, r]
                    + m.adaptation_costs_abs[t, r]
                ),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.indirect_costs,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    m.GDP_loss[t, r]
                    - (m.total_direct_costs_abs[t, r] / m.baseline_GDP[t, r])
                ),
            ),
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_indirect_costs,
                lambda m, t: (
                    m.global_GDP_loss[t]
                    - (
                        sum(m.total_direct_costs_abs[t, r] for r in m.regions)
                        / m.global_baseline_GDP[t]
                    )
                ),
            ),
        ]
    )

    return constraints

docs.title: Effort-sharing
docs.text:
Back to general structure

Effort-sharing regimes can be used to enforce the redistribution of mitigation effort and damage costs among regions following pre-defined equity principles. By default, in MIMOSA, no effort-sharing regime is imposed.

Besides no regime at all, there are five effort-sharing regimes implemented in MIMOSA. The regime can be selected using the effortsharing module parameter.

No regime defaultEqual mitigation costsEqual total costsPer capita convergenceAbility to payEqual cumulative per capita emissions

Usage: 

params = load_params()
params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "noregime"
model = MIMOSA(params)

By default, no effort-sharing regime is imposed.

Source code in mimosa/components/effortsharing/noregime.py 
def get_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    """
    Usage:
    ```python hl_lines="2"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "noregime"
    model = MIMOSA(params)
    ```

    By default, no effort-sharing regime is imposed.

    """

    return []

Usage: 

params = load_params()
params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "equal_mitigation_costs"

# Effort-sharing regimes require emission trading to be feasible:
params["model structure"]["emissiontrade module"] = "emissiontrade"

# Cost-minimisation is typically used, to allocate real mitigation effort to regions with the lowest costs:
params["model structure"]["welfare module"] = "cost_minimising"

# Often, the effort sharing regimes require financial transfers larger than the mitigation costs:
params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = -0.5

# Optionally set a carbon budget:
params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = "700 GtCO2"

model = MIMOSA(params)

Equal mitigation costs implies that the attributed mitigation costs in every year (in terms of percentage of GDP) should be the same for every region:

\[ \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::mitigation_costs}{\text{mitigation costs}_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::effort_sharing_common_level}{\text{common level}_t}, \]

where the variable \(\href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::effort_sharing_common_level}{\text{common level}_t}\) can have arbitrary values and is purely used as a common value accross all the regions1.

  1. Implementing every regional condition as an exact equality can give IPOPT too many or redundant equality equations relative to the available variables. The condition is therefore implemented as an "almost-equality" (a soft-equality constraint), allowing a difference of at most 0.5%. See Soft-equality constraints.

    \[ 0.995 \cdot \text{RHS} \leq \text{LHS} \leq 1.005 \cdot \text{RHS}. \]

    ↩

def get_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    r"""
    Usage:
    ```python hl_lines="2"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "equal_mitigation_costs"

    # Effort-sharing regimes require emission trading to be feasible:
    params["model structure"]["emissiontrade module"] = "emissiontrade"

    # Cost-minimisation is typically used, to allocate real mitigation effort to regions with the lowest costs:
    params["model structure"]["welfare module"] = "cost_minimising"

    # Often, the effort sharing regimes require financial transfers larger than the mitigation costs:
    params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = -0.5

    # Optionally set a carbon budget:
    params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = "700 GtCO2"

    model = MIMOSA(params)
    ```

    Equal mitigation costs implies that the attributed mitigation costs in every year (in terms of
    percentage of GDP) should be the same for every region:

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::mitigation_costs}{\text{mitigation costs}_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::effort_sharing_common_level}{\text{common level}_t},
    $$

    where the variable $\href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_mitigation_costs::effort_sharing_common_level}{\text{common level}_t}$ can have arbitrary values and is purely used as a common
    value accross all the regions[^1].

    [^1]: Implementing every regional condition as an exact equality can give IPOPT too many or
        redundant equality equations relative to the available variables. The condition is therefore
        implemented as an "almost-equality" (a soft-equality constraint), allowing a difference of at
        most 0.5%. See [Soft-equality constraints](../extending/variables_constraints.md#soft-equality-constraints).

        $$
        0.995 \cdot \text{RHS} \leq \text{LHS} \leq 1.005 \cdot \text{RHS}.
        $$

    """

    m.effort_sharing_common_level = Var(
        m.t,
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_GDP"),
        doc="Common mitigation-cost share of gross GDP targeted across regions. Each region's attributed mitigation-cost share is constrained to remain approximately equal to this value.",
    )

    return [
        RegionalSoftEqualityConstraint(
            lambda m, t, r: m.mitigation_costs[t, r],
            lambda m, t, r: m.effort_sharing_common_level[t],
            "effort_sharing_regime_mitigation_costs",
        ),
    ]

    \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_total_costs::mitigation_costs}{\text{mitigation costs}_{t,r}} + \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_total_costs::damage_costs}{\text{damage costs}_{t,r}}\ (+ \href{./#var__financialtransfer_globaldamagepool::financial_transfer}{\text{financial transfer}_{t,r}}) = \href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_total_costs::effort_sharing_common_level}{\text{common level}_t},
    $$

    value accross all the regions[^1]. Note that the variable $\href{./#var__effortsharing_equal_total_costs::damage_costs}{\text{damages}_{t,r}}$ is already expressed as percentage of GDP (see [Damages](damages/index.md)).

    For feasibility reasons, this constraint is only enforced until 2100.

    Compared to the equal mitigation cost regime, this regime might be infeasible, especially for regions with very high damages, unless:

    * (a) the mitigation costs can be negative (for regions with very high damages). This can be achieved with the
        parameter [`rel_mitigation_costs_min_level`](#param__economics.MAC.rel_mitigation_costs_min_level).

    * or (b) if financial transfers are allowed between regions, that go beyond emission trading. See [Financial transfers](financialtransfers.md).

        redundant equality equations relative to the available variables. The condition is therefore
        implemented as an "almost-equality" (a soft-equality constraint), allowing a difference of at

The per capita convergence regime allocates equal per capita emission rights to each region, starting from a given year (called the convergence year). The convergence year can be set with the parameter percapconv_year and is set to 2050 by default. Before this convergence year, the allowances are interpolated between grandfathering (the emission distribution in the first model year) and equal per capita emission rights in the convergence year.

Therefore, two functions are needed. First, the allowances for equal per capita emissions (EPC):

\[ \text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r} = \frac{\href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{\text{population}_{t,r}}}{\sum_{s} \href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{\text{population}_{t,s}}} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}, \]

and second the allowances for grandfathering (GF):

\[ \text{allowances}_{\text{GF}, t, r} = \frac{\href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,r}}}{\sum_{s} \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,s}}} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}, \]

Finally, each region's emission share is calculated as a linear interpolation between the two distributions before the convergence year. After the convergence year, only the equal per capita shares are used. The resulting allowances are:

\[ \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::regional_emission_allowances}{\text{allowances}_{t, r}} = \begin{cases} x \cdot \text{allowances}_{\text{GF}, t, r} + (1-x) \cdot (\text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r}), & \text{if } t < \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}}, \\ \text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r}, & \text{if } t \geq \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}},\\ \text{allowances}_{\text{GF},t,r}, & \text{if } \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}} = \text{false}. \end{cases} \]

where \(x\) is the linear interpolation factor, which is 1 in the first year and 0 in the convergence year:

\[ x = \frac{t - \href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}}{\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}} - \href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}}. \]

Finally, the calculated allowances are imposed on each region's regional_emission_allowances. Since this regime needs emission trading to avoid infeasibility, allowances are calculated from the reductions attributed to a region. These can differ from the physical reductions within that region because reductions can be traded:

\[ \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::regional_emission_allowances}{\text{allowances}_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::attributed_emission_reductions}{\text{attributed emission reductions}_{t,r}} \] Source code in mimosa/components/effortsharing/per_cap_convergence.py

    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs

    r"""
    Usage:
    ```python hl_lines="2-3"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "per_cap_convergence"
    params["effort sharing"]["percapconv_year"] = 2050

    # Effort-sharing regimes require emission trading to be feasible:
    params["model structure"]["emissiontrade module"] = "emissiontrade"

    # Cost-minimisation is typically used, to allocate real mitigation effort to regions with the lowest costs:
    params["model structure"]["welfare module"] = "cost_minimising"

    # Often, the effort sharing regimes require financial transfers larger than the mitigation costs:
    params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = -0.5

    # Optionally set a carbon budget:
    params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = "700 GtCO2"

    model = MIMOSA(params)
    ```

    The per capita convergence regime allocates equal per capita emission rights to each region, starting
    from a given year (called the convergence year). The convergence year can be set with the parameter
    [`percapconv_year`](#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year) and is
    set to 2050 by default. Before this convergence year, the allowances are interpolated
    between grandfathering (the emission distribution in the first model year) and equal per capita
    emission rights in the convergence year.


    Therefore, two functions are needed. First, the allowances for equal per capita emissions (EPC):

    $$
    \text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r} = \frac{\href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{\text{population}_{t,r}}}{\sum_{s} \href{./#param__timeandregional.population}{\text{population}_{t,s}}} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}},
    $$

    and second the allowances for grandfathering (GF):

    $$
    \text{allowances}_{\text{GF}, t, r} = \frac{\href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,r}}}{\sum_{s} \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,s}}} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}},
    $$

    :::mimosa.components.effortsharing.per_cap_convergence.percapconv_share_rule

    Finally, the calculated allowances are imposed on each region's `regional_emission_allowances`.
    Since this regime needs [emission trading](emissiontrading.md) to avoid infeasibility, allowances
    are calculated from the reductions attributed to a region. These can differ from the physical
    reductions within that region because reductions can be traded:

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::regional_emission_allowances}{\text{allowances}_{t,r}} = \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::attributed_emission_reductions}{\text{attributed emission reductions}_{t,r}}
    $$


    """
    ## Per capita convergence:
    # m.regional_per_cap_emissions = Var(
    #     m.t, m.regions, units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit/population_unit")
    # )
    m.percapconv_share_init = Param(
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, r: m.ssp_baseline_emissions[0, r]
        / sum(m.ssp_baseline_emissions[0, s] for s in m.regions),
    )
    m.percapconv_year = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("effort sharing.percapconv_year")
    )
    m.percapconv_share_pop = Param(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.population[t, r] / m.global_population[t],
    )

    m.percapconv_share = Param(m.t, m.regions, initialize=percapconv_share_rule)

    return [
        RegionalSoftEqualityConstraint(
            lambda m, t, r: m.percapconv_share[t, r] * m.global_emissions[t],
            lambda m, t, r: m.regional_emission_allowances[t, r],
            epsilon=None,
            absolute_epsilon=0.001,
            ignore_if=lambda m, t, r: t == 0,
            name="percapconv_rule",
        ),
    ]

In the equal cumulative per capita (ECPC) regime, emission allowances are allocated based on an equal per capita distribution of emissions, combining both historical and future emissions per capita. The historical emission debt is then spread out over the future time steps, going linearly down to zero in the repayment end year (default: 2050).

First, a historical debt is calculated for each region: how much more, or less, emissions did a region emit compared to its fair share of cumulative emissions per capita since a start year (by default 1850).

Effort sharing in simulation mode

The example effort-sharing runs use optimisation. In simulation mode, the effort-sharing rules are not applied directly because they are constraints on calculated variables such as regional emission allowances and mitigation costs. A simulation can replay an optimised effort-sharing result when all underlying control values, including the relevant trading balances, are supplied, but it does not determine a new effort-sharing allocation itself.

def percapconv_share_rule(m, t, r):
    r"""
    Finally, [each region's emission share](#param__timeandregional.percapconv_share) is calculated as a linear interpolation between the two distributions before the convergence year. After the convergence year,
    only the equal per capita shares are used. The resulting allowances are:

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_per_cap_convergence::regional_emission_allowances}{\text{allowances}_{t, r}} = \begin{cases}
    x \cdot \text{allowances}_{\text{GF}, t, r} + (1-x) \cdot (\text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r}), & \text{if } t < \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}}, \\
    \text{allowances}_{\text{EPC}, t, r}, & \text{if } t \geq \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}},\\
    \text{allowances}_{\text{GF},t,r}, & \text{if } \href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}} = \text{false}.
    \end{cases}
    $$

    where $x$ is the linear interpolation factor, which is 1 in the first year and 0 in the convergence year:

    $$
    x = \frac{t - \href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}}{\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.percapconv_year}{\text{convergence year}} - \href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}}.
    $$

    #### Immediate per capita convergence

    If the convergence year is set to the first year, the per capita convergence is applied immediately:

    ```python hl_lines="3"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "per_cap_convergence"
    params["effort sharing"]["percapconv_year"] = params["time"]["start"]
    ```

    #### Grandfathering

    If the convergence year is set to `false`, the grandfathering allowance distribution is used all the time.

    ```python hl_lines="3"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "per_cap_convergence"
    params["effort sharing"]["percapconv_year"] = False  # Grandfathering all the time
    ```
    """

    year_0, year_t = m.year(0), m.year(t)
    year_conv = m.percapconv_year

    if year_conv is False:
        # If it is false, use grandfathering all the time
        return m.percapconv_share_init[r]
    if year_conv == year_0:
        # If it is equal to first year, use immediate per capita convergence
        return m.percapconv_share_pop[t, r]

    year_linear_part = (year_t - year_0) / (year_conv - year_0)

    return (
        min(year_linear_part, 1) * m.percapconv_share_pop[t, r]
        + max(1 - year_linear_part, 0) * m.percapconv_share_init[r]
    )

docs.text:
\[ \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction}{\text{reductions}_{\text{AP}; t,r}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{\text{per cap. GDP}_{t,r}}{\text{global per cap. GDP}_{t}}} \cdot \text{glob. fract. of baseline emissions}_{t} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}}, \]

with

\[ \text{glob. frac. of baseline emissions}_{t} = \frac{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}}{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t}}. \]

Note: The per-capita GDP can be calculated in two ways: either from the baseline GDP parameter or from the net GDP variable. For numerical stability, we use the baseline GDP parameter, even though it would be slightly more accurate to use the net GDP variable.

def ability_to_pay_rule(m, t, r):
    r"""
    #### Step 1: Reductions before correction factor

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction}{\text{reductions}_{\text{AP}; t,r}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{\text{per cap. GDP}_{t,r}}{\text{global per cap. GDP}_{t}}} \cdot \text{glob. fract. of baseline emissions}_{t} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}},
    $$

    with

    $$
    \text{glob. frac. of baseline emissions}_{t} = \frac{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}}{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t}}.
    $$

    *Note: The per-capita GDP can be calculated in two ways: either from the [baseline GDP](#param__timeandregional.baseline_GDP) parameter or from the net GDP variable. For numerical stability, we use the [baseline GDP](#param__timeandregional.baseline_GDP) parameter, even though it would be slightly more accurate to use the net GDP variable.*


    """
    gdp_var = m.baseline_GDP  # or: m.GDP_net
    per_cap_gdp = gdp_var[t, r] / m.population[t, r]
    global_per_cap_gdp = sum(gdp_var[t, s] for s in m.regions) / m.global_population[t]
    global_baseline_emissions = sum(m.baseline_emissions[t, s] for s in m.regions)

    reductions_before_correction = (
        (per_cap_gdp / global_per_cap_gdp) ** (1 / 3)
        * (global_baseline_emissions - m.global_emissions[t])
        / global_baseline_emissions
        * m.baseline_emissions[t, r]
    )

    return reductions_before_correction

docs.title: Step 2: Global correction factor
docs.text:
The reduction factors from step 1 do not fully add up to the global emissions. There is typically a gap of a few percent. To correct this, a global correction factor is applied to the reductions:

\[ \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor}{\text{correction factor}_{t}} = \frac{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}}{\sum_{r} \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction}{\text{reductions}_{\text{AP}; t,r}}}. \]
