    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    r"""
    Usage:
    ```python hl_lines="2"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "ability_to_pay"

    # Effort-sharing regimes require emission trading to be feasible:
    params["model structure"]["emissiontrade module"] = "emissiontrade"

    # Cost-minimisation is typically used, to allocate real mitigation effort to regions with the lowest costs:
    params["model structure"]["welfare module"] = "cost_minimising"

    # Often, the effort sharing regimes require financial transfers larger than the mitigation costs:
    params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = -0.5

    # Optionally set a carbon budget:
    params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = "700 GtCO2"

    model = MIMOSA(params)
    ```

    In this effort-sharing regime, emission allowances are allocated based on per-capita GDP (see [van den Berg et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-019-02368-y)).

    There are three steps in the calculation of the allowances: (1) the main reduction calculation based on per-capita GDP,
    (2) a global correction factor to make sure that the total reductions match the global target, and (3) the final allowances calculation.


    :::mimosa.components.effortsharing.ability_to_pay.ability_to_pay_rule

    #### Step 2: Global correction factor

    The reduction factors from step 1 do not fully add up to the global emissions. There is typically a gap of a few percent. To correct this, a global correction factor is applied to the reductions:

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor}{\text{correction factor}_{t}} = \frac{\text{global baseline emissions}_{t} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}}{\sum_{r} \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction}{\text{reductions}_{\text{AP}; t,r}}}.
    $$

    #### Step 3: Final allowances calculation

    Finally, the allowances are calculated by subtracting the reductions from the baseline emissions, multiplied by the correction factor:

    $$
    \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_allowances}{\text{allowances}_{\text{AP}; t,r}} = \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction}{\text{reductions}_{\text{AP}; t,r}} \cdot \href{./#var__effortsharing_ability_to_pay::effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor}{\text{correction factor}_{t}}.
    $$


    """

    m.effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        doc="Provisional regional emission reductions under the ability-to-pay rule, before global correction. The global reduction fraction is scaled by the cube root of the region's baseline GDP per capita relative to the global average, then applied to its baseline emissions.",
    )
    m.effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor = Var(
        m.t,
        doc="Global multiplier applied to provisional ability-to-pay reductions so their sum matches the global emission reduction from baseline. Set to one at the initial time step.",
    )
    m.effortsharing_AP_allowances = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        doc="Regional emission allowances prescribed by the ability-to-pay rule, equal to baseline emissions minus the globally corrected regional reduction. These are the targets for the region's emission allowances after trading.",
    )

    return [
        RegionalEquation(
            m.effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction, ability_to_pay_rule
        ),
        GlobalEquation(
            m.effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor,
            lambda m, t: (
                (
                    sum(m.baseline_emissions[t, r] for r in m.regions)
                    - m.global_emissions[t]
                )
                / soft_min(
                    sum(
                        m.effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction[t, r]
                        for r in m.regions
                    )
                )
                if t > 0
                else 1
            ),
        ),
        RegionalEquation(
            m.effortsharing_AP_allowances,
            lambda m, t, r: (
                m.baseline_emissions[t, r]
                - m.effortsharing_AP_reductions_before_correction[t, r]
                * m.effortsharing_AP_inv_correction_factor[t]
            ),
        ),
        RegionalSoftEqualityConstraint(
            lambda m, t, r: m.effortsharing_AP_allowances[t, r],
            lambda m, t, r: m.regional_emission_allowances[t, r],
            epsilon=None,
            absolute_epsilon=0.001,
            ignore_if=lambda m, t, r: t == 0,
            name="effortsharing_AP_rule",
        ),
    ]

docs.title: Step 1: historical debt calculation
docs.text:
The historical debt is calculated as the cumulative difference between the historical fair share (based on equal per capita emissions) and the actual emissions, starting from a given start year (default: 1850) and using all historical observations available up to the first model year. The debt is discounted to that first model year, denoted by \(\href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}\) (2025 by default). If \(t_{\mathrm{hist}}\) is the final available historical observation:

\[ \href{./#param__timeandregional.effortsharing_ecpc_historical_debt}{\text{debt}_{r}} = \sum_{t=\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_start_year}{\text{start year}}}^{t_{\mathrm{hist}}} \left(\text{emissions}_{r,t} - \frac{\text{population}_{r,t}}{\text{global population}_{t}} \cdot \text{global emissions}_{t}\right) \cdot e^{-\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_discount_rate}{\text{discount rate}} \cdot (\href{./#param__time.start}{t_0} - t)}. \]

where you can set the following parameters:

  • \(\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_start_year}{\text{start year}}\) using params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_start_year"] (default: 1850),
  • \(\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_discount_rate}{\text{discount rate}}\) using params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_discount_rate"] (default: 3%/yr).

The historical debt is therefore positive for regions that emitted more than their fair share of cumulative emissions per capita, and negative for regions that emitted less than their fair share:

Source code in mimosa/components/effortsharing/equal_cumulative_per_cap.py 
def _calc_debt(m, r, all_emissions, all_population):
    r"""

    #### Step 1: historical debt calculation

    The historical debt is calculated as the cumulative difference between the historical
    fair share (based on equal per capita emissions) and the actual emissions, starting from
    a given start year (default: 1850) and using all historical observations available up to
    the first model year. The debt is discounted to that first model year, denoted by $\href{./#param__time.start}{t_0}$
    (2025 by default). If $t_{\mathrm{hist}}$ is the final available historical observation:

    $$
    \href{./#param__timeandregional.effortsharing_ecpc_historical_debt}{\text{debt}_{r}} = \sum_{t=\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_start_year}{\text{start year}}}^{t_{\mathrm{hist}}} \left(\text{emissions}_{r,t} - \frac{\text{population}_{r,t}}{\text{global population}_{t}} \cdot \text{global emissions}_{t}\right) \cdot e^{-\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_discount_rate}{\text{discount rate}} \cdot (\href{./#param__time.start}{t_0} - t)}.
    $$

    where you can set the following parameters:

    * $\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_start_year}{\text{start year}}$ using [`params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_start_year"]`](#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_start_year) (default: 1850),
    * $\href{./#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_discount_rate}{\text{discount rate}}$ using [`params["effort sharing"]["ecpc_discount_rate"]`](#param__effort%20sharing.ecpc_discount_rate) (default: 3%/yr).

    The historical debt is therefore positive for regions that emitted more than their fair share of cumulative emissions per capita, and negative for regions that emitted less than their fair share:

    ``` plotly
    {"file_path": "./assets/plots/ecpc_debt.json"}
    ```
    """
    start_year = value(m.effortsharing_ecpc_start_year)
    base_year = value(m.beginyear)

    emissions = all_emissions.loc[start_year:base_year]
    population = all_population.loc[start_year:base_year]
    global_emissions = emissions.sum(axis=1)
    global_population = population.sum(axis=1)

    years = global_population.index
    discount_factor = pd.Series(
        np.exp(-m.effortsharing_ecpc_discount_rate * (base_year - years)),
        index=years,
    )

    fair_share = population[r] / global_population * global_emissions
    cumulative_discounted_debt = ((emissions[r] - fair_share) * discount_factor).sum()

    return float(cumulative_discounted_debt)

docs.title: Step 2: future fair share (excluding historical debt repayment)
docs.text:
The future fair share for every region (excluding the historical debt) is equal to the immediate per capita convergence regime: every year, a region gets allocated a share of the global emissions based on their population share.

Source code in mimosa/components/effortsharing/equal_cumulative_per_cap.py 
def get_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    """
    Usage:
    ```python hl_lines="2"
    params = load_params()
    params["model structure"]["effortsharing module"] = "equal_cumulative_per_cap"

    # Effort-sharing regimes require emission trading to be feasible:
    params["model structure"]["emissiontrade module"] = "emissiontrade"

    # Cost-minimisation is typically used, to allocate real mitigation effort to regions with the lowest costs:
    params["model structure"]["welfare module"] = "cost_minimising"

    # Often, the effort sharing regimes require financial transfers larger than the mitigation costs:
    params["economics"]["MAC"]["rel_mitigation_costs_min_level"] = -0.5

    # Optionally set a carbon budget:
    params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"] = "700 GtCO2"

    model = MIMOSA(params)
    ```

    In the equal cumulative per capita (ECPC) regime, emission allowances are allocated based on an equal
    per capita distribution of emissions, combining both *historical* and *future* emissions per capita.
    The [historical emission debt](#param__timeandregional.effortsharing_ecpc_historical_debt) is then [spread out over the future time steps](#param__timeandregional.effortsharing_ecpc_annual_debt_repayment), going linearly down to
    zero in the repayment end year (default: 2050).

    First, a historical debt is calculated for each region: how much more, or less, emissions did a region emit
    compared to its fair share of cumulative emissions per capita since a start year (by default 1850).


    :::mimosa.components.effortsharing.equal_cumulative_per_cap._calc_debt

    #### Step 2: future fair share (excluding historical debt repayment)

    The future fair share for every region (excluding the historical debt) is equal to the immediate
    per capita convergence regime: every year, a region gets allocated a share of the global emissions
    based on their [population share](#param__timeandregional.percapconv_share_pop).

    ``` plotly
    {"file_path": "./assets/plots/ecpc_allowances.json"}
    ```


    """

    historical_emissions, historical_population = _load_data()
    m.effortsharing_ecpc_discount_rate = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("effort sharing.ecpc_discount_rate")
    )
    m.effortsharing_ecpc_start_year = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("effort sharing.ecpc_start_year")
    )
    m.effortsharing_ecpc_historical_debt = Param(
        m.t,  # Constant over time
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: _calc_debt(
            m, r, historical_emissions, historical_population
        ),
        units=quant.unit("emissions_unit"),
    )

    m.percapconv_share_pop = Param(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.population[t, r] / m.global_population[t],
    )

    m.effortsharing_ecpc_repayment_endyear = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("effort sharing.ecpc_repayment_endyear")
    )

    m.effortsharing_ecpc_annual_debt_repayment = Param(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=_calc_ecpc_annual_debt_repayment,
        units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit"),
    )

    return [
        RegionalSoftEqualityConstraint(
            lambda m, t, r: m.percapconv_share_pop[t, r] * m.global_emissions[t]
            - m.effortsharing_ecpc_annual_debt_repayment[t, r],
            lambda m, t, r: m.regional_emission_allowances[t, r],
            epsilon=None,
            absolute_epsilon=0.001,
            ignore_if=lambda m, t, r: t == 0,
            name="percapconv_rule",
        ),
    ]

docs.title: Emissions and temperature
docs.text:
Back to general structure

Baseline and mitigated emissions Temperature Carbon budget, inertia and other restrictions

The global temperature change is calculated as a linear function of cumulative emissions, with a slope given by the Transient Climate Response to CO2 Emissions (TCRE), following [Dietz et al.] who showed that this performed better than the default two-box DICE climate module.

\[ \href{./#var__temperature}{\text{temperature}_{t}} = \href{./#param__temperature.initial}{T_0} + \href{./#param__temperature.TCRE}{\text{TCRE}} \cdot \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}}, \]

where \(T_0\) is the initial temperature at the start of the run (2025 by default), and the TCRE is the Transient Climate Response to CO2 Emissions.

The initial temperature is set to 1.27°C in 2025 by default. Temperature is expressed as warming above pre-industrial levels, following the interpretation discussed by Visser et al. (2018). The TCRE is calibrated on the IPCC AR5 or AR6 reports (the median value of the TCRE is the same in the AR5 and AR6 calibration), but the distribution is different.

Calibration of the TCRE

The TCRE is calibrated on the IPCC AR5 and AR6 reports, both using the linear relation shown in the SPM figure of the WG1 report. The default value of the TCRE is 0.62°C per 1000 GtCO2 (median value of the AR5 and AR6 calibration). The 5th and 95th percentiles differ between the two calibrations, with the AR5 calibration having a wider distribution:

Percentile AR5 TCRE (°C per TtCO2) AR6 TCRE (°C per TtCO2) 5th 0.42 0.42 50th 0.62 0.62 default 95th 0.82 0.75 Calibrated on IPCC AR5Calibrated on IPCC AR6

Source: IPCC AR5 WG1 Figure SPM.10

Source: IPCC AR6 WG1 Figure SPM.10

MIMOSA allows several types of constraints on emissions: a global carbon budget, inertia constraints, limits on net negative emissions and constraints on emissions after 2100.

Source code in mimosa/components/emissions.py 
def get_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    """

    === ":octicons-cloud-24: Baseline and mitigated emissions"

        :::mimosa.components.emissions._get_emissions_constraints

    === ":fontawesome-solid-temperature-half: Temperature"

        :::mimosa.components.emissions._get_temperature_constraints

    === ":fontawesome-solid-chart-pie: Carbon budget, inertia and other restrictions"

        :::mimosa.components.emissions._get_inertia_and_budget_constraints

    """

    # First set baseline emission functions (cumulative emissions and global cumulative emissions)
    _set_baseline_emissions(m)
    constraints = (
        _get_emissions_constraints(m, inputs)
        + _get_temperature_constraints(m, inputs)
        + _get_inertia_and_budget_constraints(m, inputs)
    )

    return constraints

docs.title: Baseline emissions
docs.text:
In MIMOSA, emissions are represented by CO2 emissions only1. The emissions are calculated relative to baseline emissions: emissions that would occur in the absence of any climate policy.

There are two ways to calculate baseline emissions: either directly imported exogenously from the SSP scenarios, or calculated from the baseline carbon intensity from the SSPs. The latter accounts for the fact that in the absence of climate policy, baseline emissions would go down if the GDP goes down, and vice versa. This can be chosen with the parameter use_baseline_carbon_intensity. If this parameter is set to true, baseline emissions are calculated as:

\[ \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} = \href{./#param__timeandregional.baseline_carbon_intensity}{\text{baseline carbon intensity}_{t,r}} \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net}, t,r}} \] Baseline emissions values

docs.title: Emission reductions
docs.text:
To calculate the actual emissions per region, the baseline emissions are reduced by a relative abatement factor, which in term is determined by the Marginal Abatement Cost curve and the carbon price (see Mitigation). The regional emissions are then calculated as:

\[ \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}} = (1 - \href{./#var__mitigation_level}{\text{mitigation level}_{t,r}}) \cdot \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} \]

In the first period, reductions are assumed to be zero:

\[ \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{0,r}} = \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,r}}. \]

docs.title: Global and cumulative emissions
docs.text:
The regional emissions are aggregated to global emissions:

\[ \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} = \sum_r \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}}, \]

which are used to calculate the cumulative emissions. There are two ways to calculate them: using trapezoidal integration or by simply adding up all the years. The former is more accurate, while the latter is numerically more stable. This is chosen with the parameter cumulative_emissions_trapz.

Trapezoidal integration defaultSimple sum \[ \begin{aligned} \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}} & = \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t-1}} \\ & + \frac{\Delta t}{2} \cdot (\href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} + \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t-1}}) ,\text{for } t > 0. \end{aligned} \] \[ \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}} = \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t-1}} + \Delta t \cdot \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} \]

docs.title: Exogenous emissions pulse
docs.text: A one-off exogenous CO2 pulse can be added directly to cumulative emissions. Its amount is a stock in GtCO2, so it is independent of the model timestep. The pulse affects temperature and subsequent damages, but does not directly alter regional emissions or mitigation costs. By default its amount is zero.

docs.title: Parameters defined in this module
docs.text:
• params["emissions"]["baseline carbon intensity"]: If true, use baseline carbon intensity to calculate baseline emissions. If false, the SSP baseline emissions are used, regardless of lower GDP.. Type: bool. Default: True.
  • params["emissions"]["cumulative_emissions_trapz"]: If true, calculate cumulative emissions using trapezoidal interpolation. If false, cum. emissions are simply cum_emissions[t-1] + dt * cum_emissions[t]. This is less accurate, but better for numerical stability. For small dt the approximation is usually still acceptable.. Type: bool. Default: True.
  • params["emissions"]["pulse"]["year"]: Year in which an exogenous CO2 pulse is released. Type: int. Default: 2025. Min: 1900. Max: 2300.
  • params["emissions"]["pulse"]["amount"]: Exogenous CO2 pulse added directly to cumulative emissions. Type: quantity. Default: 0 GtCO2. Unit: emissions_unit.

  1. The effect of other greenhouse gases is implicitly accounted for in the TCRE which translates cumulative CO2 emissions into temperature change. This assumes a linear relation between CO2 emissions and other greenhouse gases. ↩

Source code in mimosa/components/emissions.py 
def _get_emissions_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    r"""
    ## Baseline emissions

    In MIMOSA, emissions are represented by CO<sub>2</sub> emissions only[^1]. The emissions are calculated
    relative to baseline emissions: emissions that would occur in the absence of any climate policy.

    There are two ways to calculate baseline emissions: either directly imported exogenously from
    the [SSP scenarios](#param__timeandregional.ssp_baseline_emissions), or calculated from the [baseline carbon intensity](#param__timeandregional.baseline_carbon_intensity) from the SSPs. The latter
    accounts for the fact that in the absence of climate policy, baseline emissions would go down if
    the GDP goes down, and vice versa. This can be chosen with the parameter [`use_baseline_carbon_intensity`](#param__emissions.baseline%20carbon%20intensity).
    If this parameter is set to true, baseline emissions are calculated as:

    $$
    \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}} = \href{./#param__timeandregional.baseline_carbon_intensity}{\text{baseline carbon intensity}_{t,r}} \cdot \href{./#var__GDP_net}{\text{GDP}_{\text{net}, t,r}}
    $$

    ??? info "Baseline emissions values"

        <div style="overflow: scroll;" markdown>
        ``` plotly
        {"file_path": "./assets/plots/baseline_emissions.json"}
        ```
        </div>

    ## Emission reductions
    To calculate the actual emissions per region, the baseline emissions are reduced by a relative
    abatement factor, which in term is determined by the Marginal Abatement Cost curve and the carbon price
    (see [Mitigation](mitigation.md)). The regional emissions are then calculated as:

    $$
    \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}} = (1 - \href{./#var__mitigation_level}{\text{mitigation level}_{t,r}}) \cdot \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t,r}}
    $$

    In the first period, reductions are assumed to be zero:

    $$
    \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{0,r}} = \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{0,r}}.
    $$

    ## Global and cumulative emissions

    The regional emissions are aggregated to global emissions:

    $$
    \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} = \sum_r \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}},
    $$

    which are used to calculate the cumulative emissions. There are two ways to calculate them:
    using trapezoidal integration or by simply adding up all the years. The former is more accurate,
    while the latter is numerically more stable. This is chosen with the parameter [`cumulative_emissions_trapz`](#param__emissions.cumulative_emissions_trapz).

    === "Trapezoidal integration `default`"

        $$
        \begin{aligned}
        \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}} & = \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t-1}} \\
        & + \frac{\Delta t}{2} \cdot (\href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} + \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t-1}}) ,\text{for } t > 0.
        \end{aligned}
        $$

    === "Simple sum"

        $$
        \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}} = \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t-1}} + \Delta t \cdot \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}}
        $$

    ## Exogenous emissions pulse

    A one-off exogenous CO<sub>2</sub> pulse can be added directly to cumulative
    emissions. Its amount is a stock in GtCO<sub>2</sub>, so it is independent of
    the model timestep. The pulse affects temperature and subsequent damages, but
    does not directly alter regional emissions or mitigation costs. By default
    its amount is zero.


    ## Parameters defined in this module
    - params["emissions"]["baseline carbon intensity"]: If true, use baseline carbon intensity to calculate baseline emissions. If false, the SSP baseline emissions are used, regardless of lower GDP.. Type: bool. Default: True.
    - params["emissions"]["cumulative_emissions_trapz"]: If true, calculate cumulative emissions using trapezoidal interpolation. If false, cum. emissions are simply cum_emissions[t-1] + dt * cum_emissions[t]. This is less accurate, but better for numerical stability. For small dt the  approximation is usually still acceptable.. Type: bool. Default: True.
    - params["emissions"]["pulse"]["year"]: Year in which an exogenous CO2 pulse is released. Type: int. Default: 2025. Min: 1900. Max: 2300.
    - params["emissions"]["pulse"]["amount"]: Exogenous CO2 pulse added directly to cumulative emissions. Type: quantity. Default: 0 GtCO2. Unit: emissions_unit.

    [^1]: The effect of other greenhouse gases is implicitly accounted for in the TCRE which
        translates cumulative CO<sub>2</sub> emissions into temperature change. This assumes a linear
        relation between CO<sub>2</sub> emissions and other greenhouse gases.
    """

    constraints = []

    m.regional_emissions = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit"),
        doc="Regional net CO2 emissions after mitigation, calculated as baseline emissions times one minus the mitigation level. Negative values represent net CO2 removal.",
    )
    m.baseline_emissions = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=lambda m, t, r: m.ssp_baseline_emissions[t, r],
        units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit"),
        doc="Regional baseline CO2 emissions (emissions before applying mitigation). Taken from the selected SSP or calculated from baseline carbon intensity and model GDP.",
    )
    m.use_carbon_intensity_for_baseline = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("emissions.baseline carbon intensity")
    )

    m.mitigation_level = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        initialize=0,
        # Initial abatement is fixed to zero after Pyomo preprocessing;
        # subsequent steps allow up to 250% of baseline emissions.
        # Note that limits on negative emissions can also be set with the parameters `global_min_level` and `regional_min_level`.
        bounds=(0, 2.5),
        units=quant.unit("fraction_of_baseline_emissions"),
        doc="Fraction of baseline emissions reduced through mitigation. Zero means no mitigation, one means net-zero emissions, and values above one represent net-negative emissions.",
    )

    # If set, delay mitigation until after a given year by setting a bound on mitigation_level:
    m.delay_mitigation_year = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("emissions.delay_mitigation_until_year")
    )
    constraints.append(
        RegionalConstraint(
            lambda m, t, r: (
                m.mitigation_level[t, r] <= 0.001
                if value(m.delay_mitigation_year) is not False
                and m.year(t) <= m.delay_mitigation_year
                else Constraint.Skip
            )
        )
    )

    m.regional_emission_reductions = Var(
        m.t,
        m.regions,
        units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit"),
        doc="Regional reduction in CO2 emissions relative to the baseline, calculated as baseline emissions minus actual net emissions. Can exceed baseline emissions when net emissions are negative.",
    )
    m.global_cumulative_emissions = Var(
        m.t,
        units=quant.unit("emissions_unit"),
        doc="Cumulative global net CO2 emissions since the model start, including any exogenous emissions pulse. Calculated using trapezoidal integration or timestep-weighted summation, depending on configuration.",
    )
    m.global_emissions = Var(
        m.t,
        units=quant.unit("emissionsrate_unit"),
        doc="Global net CO2 emissions, calculated as the sum of regional net emissions. Negative values represent net CO2 removal.",
    )

    m.global_cumulative_emissions_trapz = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("emissions.cumulative_emissions_trapz")
    )
    m.emissions_pulse_year = Param(initialize=inputs.config("emissions.pulse.year"))
    m.emissions_pulse_amount = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("emissions.pulse.amount"),
        validate=_validate_emissions_pulse,
    )

    constraints.extend(
        [
            # Baseline emissions based on emissions or carbon intensity
            RegionalEquation(
                m.baseline_emissions,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    (
                        m.baseline_carbon_intensity[t, r]
                        * (m.GDP_net[t - 1, r] if t > 1 else m.GDP_gross[t, r])
                    )
                    if value(m.use_carbon_intensity_for_baseline)
                    else m.ssp_baseline_emissions[t, r]
                ),
            ),
            # Regional emissions from baseline and mitigation level
            RegionalEquation(
                m.regional_emissions,
                lambda m, t, r: (
                    (1 - m.mitigation_level[t, r])
                    * (
                        m.baseline_emissions[t, r]
                        if value(m.use_carbon_intensity_for_baseline)
                        else m.ssp_baseline_emissions[t, r]
                    )
                ),
            ),
            RegionalEquation(
                m.regional_emission_reductions,
                lambda m, t, r: m.baseline_emissions[t, r] - m.regional_emissions[t, r],
            ),
            # Global emissions (sum from regional emissions)
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_emissions,
                lambda m, t: sum(m.regional_emissions[t, r] for r in m.regions),
            ),
            # Cumulative emissions
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_cumulative_emissions,
                lambda m, t: (
                    (
                        m.global_cumulative_emissions[t - 1]
                        + (
                            (
                                m.period_length[t]
                                * (m.global_emissions[t] + m.global_emissions[t - 1])
                                / 2
                            )
                            if value(m.global_cumulative_emissions_trapz)
                            else (m.period_length[t] * m.global_emissions[t])
                        )
                        if t > 0
                        else 0
                    )
                    + (
                        m.emissions_pulse_amount
                        if m.year(t) == value(m.emissions_pulse_year)
                        else 0
                    )
                ),
            ),
        ]
    )

    m.global_relative_cumulative_emissions = Var(
        m.t,
        initialize=1,
        doc="Cumulative global CO2 emissions divided by cumulative SSP baseline emissions since the model start. Set to one at the initial timestep.",
    )
    constraints.extend(
        [
            GlobalEquation(
                m.global_relative_cumulative_emissions,
                lambda m, t: (
                    m.global_cumulative_emissions[t]
                    / m.global_cumulative_baseline_emissions[t]
                    if t > 0
                    else 1
                ),
            ),
        ]
    )

    return constraints

docs.title: Temperature target
docs.text:
The usual way to specify a policy target in MIMOSA is using carbon budgets. However, it is also possible to specify a temperature target. This is done by setting the parameter temperature_target. This is an upper bound on the temperature: if the cost-optimal temperature is below this value, this constraint is not binding.

If this parameter is set, the following constraint is active:

\[ \href{./#var__temperature}{\text{temperature}_{t}} \leq \href{./#param__temperature.target}{\text{temperature target}} \]

• params["temperature"]["initial"]: Temperature in initial year of model run (2025 by default).. Type: quantity. Default: 1.27 delta_degC. Unit: temperature_unit.
  • params["temperature"]["TCRE"]: Transient Climate Response to CO2 Emissions. Type: quantity. Default: 0.62 delta_degC/(TtCO2). Unit: (temperature_unit)/(emissions_unit).
  • params["temperature"]["target"]: Temperature target in 2100 (and beyond). Can also be false, then no temperature target is imposed. Type: quantity. Default: False. Can also be false. Unit: temperature_unit.

def _get_temperature_constraints(
    m: ConcreteModel, inputs: ModelInputs
) -> Sequence[GeneralConstraint]:
    r"""

    The global temperature change is calculated as a linear function of cumulative emissions, with a slope
    given by the Transient Climate Response to CO<sub>2</sub> Emissions (TCRE), following [Dietz et al.] who
    showed that this performed better than the default two-box DICE climate module.

    $$
    \href{./#var__temperature}{\text{temperature}_{t}} = \href{./#param__temperature.initial}{T_0} + \href{./#param__temperature.TCRE}{\text{TCRE}} \cdot \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}},
    $$

    where [$T_0$](#param__temperature.initial) is the initial temperature at the start of the run (2025 by default),
    and the [TCRE](#param__temperature.TCRE) is the Transient Climate Response to CO<sub>2</sub> Emissions.

    The initial temperature is set to 1.27°C in 2025 by default. Temperature is expressed as warming above
    pre-industrial levels, following the interpretation discussed by
    [Visser et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-14-139-2018). The TCRE
    is calibrated on the IPCC AR5 or AR6 reports (the median value of the TCRE is the same in the AR5
    and AR6 calibration), but the distribution is different.

    ??? info "Calibration of the TCRE"

        The TCRE is calibrated on the IPCC AR5 and AR6 reports, both using the linear relation shown in the SPM figure of the WG1 report.
        The default value of the TCRE is 0.62°C per 1000 GtCO<sub>2</sub> (median value of the AR5 and AR6 calibration). The 5th and 95th percentiles
        differ between the two calibrations, with the AR5 calibration having a wider distribution:

        | Percentile | AR5 TCRE <br><span style="font-weight: normal">(°C per TtCO<sub>2</sub>)</span> | AR6 TCRE <br><span style="font-weight: normal">(°C per TtCO<sub>2</sub>)</span> |
        |------------|----------|----------|
        | 5th        | 0.42     | 0.42     |
        | 50th       | 0.62     | 0.62 `default` |
        | 95th       | 0.82     | 0.75     |

        === "Calibrated on IPCC AR5"

            <div style="overflow: scroll;" markdown>
            ``` plotly
            {"file_path": "./assets/plots/ar5_tcre.json"}
            ```
            </div>
            Source: [IPCC AR5 WG1 Figure SPM.10](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar5/wg1/summary-for-policymakers/figspm-10/)

        === "Calibrated on IPCC AR6"

            <div style="overflow: scroll;" markdown>
            ``` plotly
            {"file_path": "./assets/plots/ar6_tcre.json"}
            ```
            </div>

            Source: [IPCC AR6 WG1 Figure SPM.10](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/figures/summary-for-policymakers/figure-spm-10)

    ## Temperature target
    The usual way to specify a policy target in MIMOSA is using carbon budgets. However, it is also possible to
    specify a temperature target. This is done by setting the parameter [`temperature_target`](#param__temperature.target).
    This is an upper bound on the temperature: if the cost-optimal temperature is below this value, this constraint is not binding.

    If this parameter is set, the following constraint is active:

    $$
    \href{./#var__temperature}{\text{temperature}_{t}} \leq \href{./#param__temperature.target}{\text{temperature target}}
    $$

    ## Parameters defined in this module
    - params["temperature"]["initial"]: Temperature in initial year of model run (2025 by default).. Type: quantity. Default: 1.27 delta_degC. Unit: temperature_unit.
    - params["temperature"]["TCRE"]: Transient Climate Response to CO2 Emissions. Type: quantity. Default: 0.62 delta_degC/(TtCO2). Unit: (temperature_unit)/(emissions_unit).
    - params["temperature"]["target"]: Temperature target in 2100 (and beyond). Can also be false, then no temperature target is imposed. Type: quantity. Default: False. Can also be false. Unit: temperature_unit.
    """

    constraints = []

    m.T0 = Param(
        units=quant.unit("degC_above_PI"),
        initialize=inputs.config("temperature.initial"),
    )
    m.temperature = Var(
        m.t,
        initialize=lambda m, t: m.T0,
        units=quant.unit("degC_above_PI"),
        doc="Global mean warming above pre-industrial levels. Calculated as initial warming plus the temperature response to cumulative CO2 emissions, determined by the TCRE.",
    )
    m.TCRE = Param(initialize=inputs.config("temperature.TCRE"))
    m.temperature_target = Param(initialize=inputs.config("temperature.target"))
    constraints.extend(
        [
            GlobalEquation(
                m.temperature,
                lambda m, t: (
                    m.T0 + m.TCRE * m.global_cumulative_emissions[t] if t > 0 else m.T0
                ),
            ),
            GlobalConstraint(
                lambda m, t: (
                    m.temperature[t] <= m.temperature_target
                    if (m.year(t) >= 2100 and value(m.temperature_target) is not False)
                    else Constraint.Skip
                ),
                name="temperature_target",
            ),
        ]
    )

    m.perc_reversible_damages = Param(
        initialize=inputs.config("economics.damages.percentage reversible")
    )

    # m.overshoot = Var(m.t, initialize=0)
    # m.overshootdot = DerivativeVar(m.overshoot, wrt=m.t)
    # m.netnegative_emissions = Var(m.t)
    # global_constraints.extend(
    #     [
    #         lambda m, t: m.netnegative_emissions[t]
    #         == m.global_emissions[t] * (1 - tanh(m.global_emissions[t] * 10)) / 2
    #         if value(m.perc_reversible_damages) < 1
    #         else Constraint.Skip,
    #         lambda m, t: m.overshootdot[t]
    #         == (m.netnegative_emissions[t] if m.year(t) <= 2100 and t > 0 else 0)
    #         if value(m.perc_reversible_damages) < 1
    #         else Constraint.Skip,
    #     ]
    # )

    # global_constraints_init.extend([lambda m: m.overshoot[0] == 0])

    return constraints

docs.title: Carbon budget
docs.text:
By default, the carbon budget is set to False, which means that MIMOSA runs in CBA mode without carbon budget. If a carbon budget is defined using the parameter carbonbudget, the following constraint is active:

\[ \href{./#var__global_cumulative_emissions}{\text{cumulative emissions}_{t}} - \href{./#param__emissions.carbonbudget}{\text{budget}} \leq 0, \]

for \(t \geq 2100\). Note that the carbonbudget parameter unit should be in GtCO2 (or TtCO2 or MtCO2).

docs.title: Inertia
docs.text:
In MIMOSA, there is a limit on how fast emissions can be reduced. This constraint is called inertia, and represents the technological, social, political and economic difficulties of quickly reducing emissions. It is implemented as a hard limit on the speed of emission reductions. The parameters inertia_global and inertia_regional are defined as percentages of baseline emissions in the initial year. If baseline emissions in a region are 10 GtCO2/yr in the initial year, and the global inertia is 5%, then the global emissions cannot be reduced by more than 0.5 GtCO2/yr throughout the whole run. This way, the parameter is independent of the size of the region.

Global inertiaRegional inertia \[ \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} - \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t-1}} \geq \Delta t \cdot \href{./#param__emissions.inertia.global}{\text{inertia_global}} \cdot \text{scaling factor}, \]

with the scaling factor the global baseline emissions in the starting year:

\[ \text{scaling factor} = \left( \sum_r \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t=0,r}}\right) \]

By default, the inertia_global is set to False, such that there is no global inertia constraint. The only inertia constraint happens regionally by default.

\[ \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t-1,r}} \geq \Delta t \cdot \href{./#param__emissions.inertia.regional}{\text{inertia_regional}} \cdot \href{./#var__baseline_emissions}{\text{baseline emissions}_{t=0,r}}. \]

By default, the inertia_regional parameter is active, such that regional emissions cannot be reduced by more than 5% of the initial baseline emissions per year. This is based on maximum reduction speeds in scenarios underpinning the IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C, as analysed by Hof et al. (2021).

docs.title: Minimum emission levels (limits to net-negative emissions)
docs.text:
Since the Marginal Abatement Cost curve is a continuous function with no upper bound, reductions can theoretically be without bound. To still address the difficulties associated with CDR technologies, a limit on (net) negative emissions can be imposed. These difficulties can be economic (e.g., land becoming increasingly scarce or increased dependence on expensive storage sites) or socio-political (e.g., concerns about biodiversity and food security). These restrictions and side effects are discussed by Hof et al. (2021) and Fuss et al. (2018). By default, global emissions are limited to -20 GtCO2/yr, and regional emissions to -10 GtCO2/yr:

\[ \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_t} \geq \href{./#param__emissions.global%20min%20level}{\text{global min level}}, \] \[ \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_t} \geq \href{./#param__emissions.regional%20min%20level}{\text{regional min level}}. \]

Note that currently, the minimum regional emission level is the same for every region, but this could be easily changed if needed (see Extending MIMOSA).

docs.title: Constraints on emissions after 2100
docs.text:
In CBA mode, it can be useful to run MIMOSA until 2150 instead of 2100, to avoid end-of-horizon effects. One way to mitigate this effect is to impose a constraint on the growth of emissions after 2100. By default, emissions are not allowed to grow after 2100:

\[ \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t,r}} - \href{./#var__regional_emissions}{\text{regional emissions}_{t-1,r}} \leq 0, \text{if } t - 1 > 2100, \]

if the parameter non_increasing_emissions_after_2100 is set to True.

When a carbon budget is imposed, it is also possible to impose a net-zero emissions constraint after the budget year (2100):

$$ \href{./#var__global_emissions}{\text{global emissions}_{t}} \leq 0, \text{if } t \geq 2100, $$ if the parameter no_pos_emissions_after_budget_year is set to True, and if a carbon budget is specified. Otherwise, this constraint is ignored.

docs.title: Parameters defined in this module
docs.text:
• params["emissions"]["carbonbudget"]: Value of the carbon budget. Example: "800 GtCO2" (the unit is important). If set to False, no carbon budget is imposed: this is cost-benefit mode. Default: False.. Type: quantity. Default: False. Can also be false. Unit: emissions_unit.
  • params["emissions"]["inertia"]["global"]: Maximum reduction speed, in % of initial emissions (should be negative) Can also be false, then no inertia limit is imposed. Type: float. Default: False. Can also be false. Min: -inf. Max: 0.
  • params["emissions"]["inertia"]["regional"]: Maximum reduction speed, in % of initial emissions (should be negative) Can also be false, then no inertia limit is imposed. Type: float. Default: -0.05. Can also be false. Min: -inf. Max: 0.
  • params["emissions"]["global min level"]: Limit on the emission level (globally), mostly used for negative emissions. Can also be false, then no limit is imposed. Type: quantity. Default: -20 GtCO2/yr. Can also be false. Unit: emissionsrate_unit.
  • params["emissions"]["regional min level"]: Limit on the emission level (per region), mostly used for negative emissions. Can also be false, then no limit is imposed. Type: quantity. Default: -10 GtCO2/yr. Can also be false. Unit: emissionsrate_unit.
  • params["emissions"]["not positive after budget year"]: If true, impose net-zero emissions after budget year (2100). Type: bool. Default: True.
  • params["emissions"]["non increasing emissions after 2100"]: If true, the regional emissions after 2100 are not allowed to climb.. Type: bool. Default: True.
